title: How Many People Can One Boss Handle? | Principles of Management Ep 27
description:
How many people can one manager really handle? Chai Corner now has five outlets and thirty people, and all thirty still report straight to Ravi. Answers take days, mistakes go unseen, and Ravi falls behind. In this animated lesson we watch the same thirty people re-arrange into a fan, a tall chart and a flat chart.

You will learn what span of control means (also called span of management: the number of people one manager can supervise well), how a narrow span creates a tall structure (close supervision, but slow messages and more managers) and how a wide span creates a flat structure (more freedom and fast messages, but staff must be skilled). We also cover the 5 factors that set the right span: the nature of the work, the skill of the manager and staff, the need for supervision, communication technology, and geographic spread.

This is Episode 27 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Thirty people, one boss
0:23 What is span of control?
0:35 Giving every outlet a manager
0:49 Narrow span vs wide span: tall and flat charts
1:08 Pros and cons of tall and flat structures
1:23 5 factors that decide the span
1:57 Ravi's choice
2:10 Quick check
2:23 Recap

Next episode: Organizational Effectiveness, the series finale.
